articles.title: China Secures Massive Discount on Russian Gas as Moscow's Leverage Weakens - Crude Oil Prices Today | OilPrice.com
articles.summary: China Secures Massive Discount on Russian Gas as Moscow's Leverage Weakens  Crude Oil Prices Today | OilPrice.com
articles.full_text:
Russia is giving China a huge discount on natural gas purchases, underscoring the Kremlin’s fiscal dependency on Beijing.
The Moscow Times (MT), citing Russian Duma documentation, shows that China will pay an average of approximately $248 per thousand cubic meters of pipeline gas in 2026, compared with $562 for Gazprom's other foreign customers outside the former Soviet Union.
That means Beijing is receiving as much as a 56 percent discount on its purchase price.
The steep discount appears to be the cost of Beijing’s ongoing political support for the Kremlin’s war effort in Ukraine.
Given the Western sanctions regime and the European Union’s efforts to reduce its reliance on Russian gas, China’s purchases are a crucial source of funds needed to keep Russia’s war machine going.
Russia hopes to reduce the discounts in the coming years, according to the MT report.
To put Russia’s weak negotiating position into context, an estimate published by Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center showed China is paying up to $60 per tcm more to Turkmenistan than the Russian purchase price.
Meanwhile, talks of creating a “Power of Siberia 2” pipeline have stalled over a pricing dispute, according to Beijing-connected media reports.
“It’s much harder for Russian negotiators today,” Sergei Vakulenko, a senior fellow at Carnegie, wrote in the estimate.
“On the one hand, the growing confrontation between the United States and China, and the instability in the Middle East, should push China into reducing LNG imports in favor of pipeline gas, which would likely be to Moscow’s advantage,” Vakulenko stated.
“On the other hand, the break with Europe has left Gazprom with huge gas reserves in Siberia’s Yamal Peninsula that are ready to be exploited but have no customers, significantly strengthening China’s position.
”
Central Asia
Chinese Premier Li Qiang traveled to Central Asia on October 17-19, visiting Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. The tour produced deals with both Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, including for a non-ferrous metallurgy industrial cluster in the Sughd region. For more about Li’s visit, see this Eurasianet report.
China’s Institute of East European, Russian, and Central Asian Studies (IREECAS), a major government think tank that informs Beijing’s regional policymaking, co-organized a China-Central Asia forum in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek for regional scholars and experts. The meeting focused on the “preparation of practical recommendations” for regional governments on a wide range of domestic and international policies. IREECAS also held a joint event with Uzbekistan’s presidential think tank, ISRS, in Tashkent, focusing on government efforts to promote artificial intelligence and digital transformation. At the conclusion of the gathering, IREECAS and ISRS announced the signing of a program of joint events and initiatives for 2027. IREECAS’s activities fit into China’s growing push to exert influence on the direction of Central Asian states’ domestic and international policymaking.
Kazakhstan
Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev launched construction of a $1.
8 billion copper smelter at the Aktogay deposit in Kazakhstan’s Abai region.
The project, developed by Kazakh mining company KAZ Minerals, with NFC, a subsidiary of China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC), is designed to produce 300,000 tons of copper cathodes annually, alongside gold and sulfuric acid, and is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs.
First production is scheduled for 2030.
Tokayev separately met with CNMC Chairman Wen Gang, who pledged to complete construction on schedule and expand cooperation in workforce training.
However, a Chinese corporate disclosure dated October 21 indicates that NFC’s Kazakh entity has signed only a preparatory-work agreement, capped at 4.
52 billion tenge (about $10 million), and that the full construction contract remains unsigned.
KAZ Minerals and NFC also signed a memorandum of understanding on geological exploration and mineral-resource assessment in Kazakhstan, according to the official state news agency Kazinform.
The companies plan to explore the use of remote sensing, geophysical and geochemical surveys, artificial intelligence, and three-dimensional geological modeling to reassess historical geological data and identify potential drilling sites.
The memorandum also provides for possible specialist training, joint research, and educational programs, with a cooperation roadmap to be developed.
No financial commitments, specific exploration sites, or implementation deadlines were disclosed.

Kazakhstan’s national investment holding Baiterek JSC announced the signing of an MoU with the Chinese firm Guoyou Materials Group covering a $1 billion investment to develop the port of Kuryk, a major Middle Corridor hub on the Caspian Sea’s Kazakh shore. The project’s first phase envisions the creation of a multifunctional terminal with a capacity of 15 million tons of cargo per year.
Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation reported that 25 Kazakh water-sector specialists are currently participating in training programs in China focused on irrigation modernization, water-saving technologies, digital water management, and small hydropower.
Kazakhstan’s Committee for National Security (KNB) reported that it detained 13 Chinese nationals allegedly operating an international online fraud scheme out of Kazakhstan that targeted individuals in other countries. The KNB officials noted that they conducted their investigation jointly with China’s Ministry of Public Security, which identified some suspects as wanted for similar offenses in China. All 13 suspects were transferred to Chinese custody to await prosecution.
Kazakhstan received observer status in the China-initiated Alliance for Cultural Heritage in Asia, according to Kazinform. Some observers see the organization as designed to advance state-led historical narratives and promote the strategic use of cultural heritage as a diplomatic tool. Kazakhstan proposed expanding cooperation in the sphere of specialist training, AI-assisted monitoring of cultural heritage sites and joint archaeological research along the Silk Road. No specific funding commitments or projects were announced.
Uzbekistan
Uzbekistan’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry held an economic conference in Tashkent with a delegation from the Chinese city of Shihezi in Xinjiang Province to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation, investment, and joint projects. The conference yielded several agreements covering logistics, construction, energy, and technology sectors. No details were immediately disclosed.
China is trying to take some energy-sector business away from Russia. The heads of Uzbekistan’s largest state-run oil and gas company, Uzbekneftegaz, and China’s largest oil and gas producer, CNPC, held talks in Tashkent to discuss expanding energy-sector cooperation. CNPC expressed readiness to help Uzbekneftegaz diversify petroleum product supplies and establish a permanent representative office in Tashkent. Russia has reduced its supply of oil-based products to Central Asian states in recent months, due to the destruction of energy infrastructure by Ukrainian drones.
Tajikistan
Tajikistan’s national telecom operator, Tajiktelecom, and the PRC’s largest telecom operator, China Mobile, launched the Tajikistan-China International Digital Corridor, a fiber-optic line that runs 1,010 km from Dushanbe through Khorog to the Kulma Pass, where it joins China Mobile’s 6,100 km network to Beijing, Tajik authorities report. The initial capacity is 1 Tbps, but it is expected to rise to 10 Tbps in the coming years. Tajikistan sees it as a step toward its ambition of becoming a hub of the Digital Silk Road and a leading regional AI player.
Tajikistan’s Ministry of Energy and Water Resources signed an MoU with Xinjiang Shouhai Power Development, a Chinese energy company, to explore the hydropower potential of the Obihingou River, Tajikistan’s official news agency Khovar reports. According to a Soviet-era assessment, the river has an estimated annual hydropower-generating capacity of 2.6 gigawatts.
Turkmenistan
Ashgabat hosted a trade and economic forum involving companies from the PRC’s Shanxi Province, Orient.tm reports. The forum resulted in the signing of two comparatively minor contracts between Turkmen and Chinese companies.

articles.title: Equinor warns Europe is vulnerable to winter gas price spike if cold weather hits - BOE Report
articles.summary: Equinor warns Europe is vulnerable to winter gas price spike if cold weather hits  BOE Report
articles.full_text:
Europe could face another spike in gas prices if cold weather boosts demand later this winter, when stocks are depleted and the region depends more on attracting scarce liquefied natural gas cargoes, Equinor’s CEO Anders Opedal said on Wednesday.
The warning came after the Norwegian gas producer reported its highest quarterly earnings since 2022, largely driven by a jump in natural gas as well as oil prices this year.
“Storage levels are at their lowest for this time of year since 2011, and there will be competition for LNG between Asia and Europe, especially if the weather turns cold,” Opedal told a press conference.
A cold spell towards the end of the heating season, when gas storage will likely be at its lowest, could lead to significant price volatility, Opedal told Reuters, though he said actual prices were impossible to predict.
Europe’s benchmark gas price has more than tripled this year to its highest levels since the 2022 energy crisis, after the US-Israeli war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting about 20% of global LNG supplies.
European gas storage sites, which help cover higher demand in winter, were at a historic low of only 75% full at the start of the heating season.
Norway is Europe’s single largest natural gas supplier via an extensive pipeline network linking its production directly with customers on the continent and Britain.
Equinor also sells LNG from its own Hammerfest plant in Norway and has signed contracts for US LNG supply, including a deal with Cheniere for 1.75 million metric tons per year.
“The Cheniere contract has now started up, meaning that we also have more LNG cargoes,” Opedal told Reuters. “Some of it goes to Europe; some of it goes to other places,” he said.
(Reporting by Nora Buli, editing by Terje Solsvik and Elaine Hardcastle)

articles.title: BTC in new bull market, could see $150K in 2027: Utkarsh Ahuja, Moon Pursuit Capital - Invezz
articles.summary: BTC in new bull market, could see $150K in 2027: Utkarsh Ahuja, Moon Pursuit Capital  Invezz
articles.full_text:
powered by
Buy Bitcoin exposure (BTC spot or a BTC ETF). The article calls for a new bull market with a gradual recovery, driven most by improving global liquidity and institutional flows, plus growing acceptance as a strategic allocation. The 2027 range ($120K–$150K) is the upside case if liquidity stays supportive and regulation doesn’t break custody/stablecoin/institutional access.
Key Risk: Liquidity tightens or institutional inflows reverse hard, pushing BTC back into a prolonged drawdown.
Buy Hyperliquid (HYPE). The thesis is 2027 rewards altcoins with real economic activity and token value accrual, not pure hype. Hyperliquid has decentralized derivatives revenue and a token buyback mechanism, so if crypto liquidity improves and trading volumes rise, cashflow-linked demand should compound.
Key Risk: Trading activity and revenue fail to grow (or volumes migrate to competitors), making buybacks too small to matter.
- Expect BTC to reach $85,000-$100,000 by 2026-end, and potentially $120,000-$150,000 in 2027.
- Expect some overinvestment in AI to become apparent in 2027.
- AI concentrating venture capital into a relatively small number of companies.
2026 saw cryptocurrency entering a bear market while the AI trade continued to grow rapidly, despite fears around AI spending causing much volatility.
Utkarsh Ahuja, managing partner and founder at Moon Pursuit Capital, a Miami-based investment firm focused on digital assets, AI, and emerging technologies, says that while the worst for crypto is over, he would not expect an explosive rally but a gradual recovery, as he sees Bitcoin closing the year between $ 85,000 and $100,000.
The firm has recently launched a $100 million market-neutral quantitative crypto fund and co-led an $8 million seed round for AmericanFortress, which is developing quantum-resistant blockchain security infrastructure.
In an interview with Invezz, Ahuja also holds forth on his forecast for Bitcoin and altcoins for 2027, the rotation of capital from crypto into AI, why he expects some overinvestment in AI to become apparent in 2027, and how AI is changing the way institutions deploy capital.
Excerpts:
Worst over for crypto; expect gradual recovery
Invezz: It has been a rough year for crypto. Do you think the worst is over? What’s your forecast for where Bitcoin could end up by the end of 2026?
I believe we’ve moved past the bottom of this corrective cycle and entered the early stages of a new bull market.
That doesn’t necessarily mean an explosive rally.
I expect a more gradual recovery, with periods of consolidation and occasional pullbacks, but the broader trajectory has shifted upward.
My base case is that Bitcoin finishes 2026 between $85,000 and $100,000, supported by improving liquidity conditions and stabilizing institutional flows.
Bitcoin’s deeper institutional investor base provides a stronger foundation for long-term demand, although volatility and historical market cycles will continue to influence price movements.
BTC could head into 2027 with a potential price range of $120,000- $150,000
Invezz: What is your outlook for Bitcoin in 2027, and which variables will matter most: interest rates, global liquidity, institutional flows or regulatory developments?
I’m constructive on Bitcoin heading into 2027, with a potential price range of $120,000 to $150,000 as the new bull market develops.
I expect the recovery to be gradual rather than a straight-line rally.
Global liquidity will be the most important driver, followed by institutional capital flows.
Regulation remains critical for long-term adoption, particularly around custody, stablecoins, and institutional participation, but favourable policies alone won’t sustain a rally without supportive monetary conditions.
I also expect Bitcoin’s growing acceptance as a strategic portfolio allocation among institutions and family offices to become an increasingly important source of demand.
Why Hyperliquid, Solana, Zcash could shine in 2027
Invezz: Which altcoins could be the big winners in 2027?
I believe 2027 will increasingly reward altcoins demonstrating real economic activity, sustainable revenue, and meaningful token value accrual rather than speculative narratives.
Hyperliquid is particularly compelling given its strong position in decentralized derivatives trading, substantial revenue generation, and token buyback mechanism.
Solana also remains interesting, although its reliance on memecoin-driven activity highlights the importance of transitioning toward more sustainable applications such as payments, DeFi, and tokenization.
I’m also bullish on privacy-focused blockchain technologies as institutional adoption increases the need for transaction confidentiality.
Zcash could benefit from this trend, although its significant recent appreciation warrants caution.
Ultimately, I favor decentralized financial infrastructure, tokenization and privacy technologies, with a particular focus on projects where growing adoption translates into tangible value for token holders.
Rotation away from crypto into AI is not permanent
Invezz: We witnessed a significant rotation of institutional and speculative money away from crypto this year into AI stocks. Do you expect this trend to continue next year? Which sectors of the AI buildout are firms like yours betting on most?
AI will likely continue attracting substantial institutional capital in 2027, driven by significant investment from hyperscalers, enterprises, and governments.
However, I don’t believe the rotation away from crypto is permanent, particularly as liquidity conditions improve and investors regain an appetite for risk.
Within AI, I see compelling opportunities in infrastructure, particularly semiconductors, power generation, grid infrastructure, networking and cooling technologies.
The biggest constraints on AI growth extend beyond computing power to electricity, connectivity and efficient deployment.
I favor businesses addressing these bottlenecks with sustainable demand, pricing power and disciplined capital expenditure.
On AI spending and the future of neoclouds
Invezz: AI infrastructure companies are committing enormous sums to chips and data centers, often relying on debt and external financing. We are all seeing the debate around neoclouds play out. Which side of the debate do you find yourself on? Do you see risks of overinvestment, and how might that affect the broader technology investment landscape in 2027? Do you think it will lead to more concentration in AI trade among some select mega-cap tech companies and hyperscalers?
I’m bullish on long-term AI computing demand, but investors need to distinguish between strong underlying demand and the financing structures supporting infrastructure expansion.
Neoclouds offer valuable flexibility, but financing rapidly depreciating GPUs with substantial debt creates risks, particularly when utilization and future pricing remain uncertain.
I expect some overinvestment to become apparent in 2027, potentially leading to consolidation as financially stronger operators acquire assets from overleveraged competitors.
This could further favor hyperscalers with cheaper access to capital, while creating opportunities for specialized operators with contracted revenue, disciplined deployment and sustainable cost advantages.
How AI is rewriting rules of institutional investment
Invezz: AI has changed the investment patterns of VCs. For example, some VCs are invested in both OpenAI and Anthropic, breaking away from the trend of not betting on rival startups. What is driving this, and can you list some other ways in which the AI boom is rewriting the rules of institutional investment?
Investors backing competing AI companies reflects both the enormous scale of the opportunity and uncertainty over which businesses will ultimately dominate.
Technological leadership can shift quickly, making concentrated exposure to a single foundation-model provider increasingly risky.
AI is also concentrating venture capital into a relatively small number of companies, with funding rounds approaching the scale traditionally associated with public markets.
We’re seeing greater overlap between venture capital, growth equity, infrastructure financing and strategic corporate investment.
Going forward, investors will place greater emphasis on computing economics, proprietary data, customer retention and sustainable profitability rather than growth alone.
Anthropic IPO an important milestone for AI, but valuation debate to remain alive
Invezz: What’s your take on Anthropic’s IPO?
Anthropic’s potential IPO represents an important milestone for AI, offering public-market investors an opportunity to evaluate a leading foundation-model company through the lens of financial performance and capital efficiency.
Its reported enterprise adoption demonstrates substantial commercial demand, but the key questions concern gross margins, inference costs, capital requirements, and the ability to convert rapid revenue growth into sustainable free cash flow.
The valuation debate will be particularly interesting: should Anthropic command software-style multiples, infrastructure-style valuations, or something in between?
I’m bullish on long-term institutional demand for AI, but even exceptional companies can become poor investments at excessive valuations.
On Moon Pursuit Capital's $100M quantitative crypto fund
Invezz: Moon Pursuit recently launched a $100 million market-neutral quantitative crypto fund. What market opportunity or investor demand prompted the launch?
We’re preparing to launch a $100 million market-neutral quantitative crypto fund in response to growing institutional demand for liquidity, capital flexibility, and consistent, risk-adjusted returns without relying on directional cryptocurrency exposure.
Liquidity has become particularly important as substantial institutional capital remains tied up in longer-duration private investments.
Investors increasingly want strategies

articles.title: Fed Rate Decision: The Fed leaves interest rates where they were - Stock Titan
articles.summary: Fed Rate Decision: The Fed leaves interest rates where they were  Stock Titan
articles.full_text:
Fed Rate Decision: Fed Holds Interest Rates at 3.75% to 4%, Caught Between Prices and Jobs
The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, with 2 of 12 voters preferring another hike, and Warsh said one 2027 meeting will set no rate. Its rate sits barely above 3.7% consumer price inflation, while job growth before September’s hike was, by our count, weaker than before any of 51 earlier increases since 1994.
The short answer. The Federal Reserve kept its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28 in a 10 to 2 vote. That leaves the Fed caught between inflation and hiring: its rate sits barely above consumer price inflation and further above core PCE inflation, which leaves out food and energy. Payroll growth of 0.34% in the year before the September hike was weaker than before any of the Fed’s 51 earlier increases since 1994, by our count, though lower immigration means fewer new jobs are needed. For borrowers, the average 30-year mortgage rate had already risen to 7.32% by October 22, from 7.03% on September 24.
What did the Fed decide at the October Fed meeting?
The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4%. The vote was 10-2, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voting for a raise.
The October 28 statement, approved 10 to 2, says “The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.” The statement adds: “Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.”
A sentence the September statement did not have says “The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal.” The statement does not say what the next move will be. It also now says economic activity is expanding at a “strong” pace, where September said “solid.”
The statement drops September’s line that “Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal,” which described that month’s hike, and keeps “The Committee will deliver price stability.” The implementation note keeps the rate banks earn on reserves at 3.90% and the primary credit rate at 4.0%, which is what the Fed charges banks for short-term loans. Its instructions to the New York Fed’s trading desk repeat September’s rates and Treasury bill purchases.

Source: Federal Reserve statements of September 16 and October 28, 2026, and the October 28 implementation note.
That leaves the range where the September hike put it. The next scheduled meeting is December 8-9, when officials also publish new projections.
What did Warsh say about rates and the Fed meeting schedule?
Warsh said inflation is still too high and that borrowing conditions have tightened since September without being tight. He also announced that from 2027 one of the Fed’s eight meetings a year will set no interest rate.
Warsh called it the Fed’s “responsibility to get inflation down” in his opening remarks, according to the Fed’s preliminary transcript. On the hike’s effect so far, he said “overall financial conditions are tighter,” but he was “unwilling and unable to call them tight.” On what comes next, he echoed the statement: “The information we receive over the coming period will help us determine where we want policy to be.”
He read the job market more warmly than our count of the year before the hike does. “So on the employment side of the Fed’s dual mandate, conditions are quite positive,” he said, adding that “payroll growth is noticeably above last year’s pace.” In our reading, both can hold, since his comparison is with last year and ours is with the years before past hikes.
The news was the calendar. Warsh said “in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated.” For 2028 he said he expects “two meetings dedicated to discussions of strategy, and six for setting policy.” With the eight meetings a year he called the right number, that would leave seven that set rates in 2027, by our arithmetic.
Where was the Fed interest rate before the October meeting?
Going into the meeting, the Fed’s target range was 3.75% to 4%. It got there on September 16, when the Fed raised rates for the first time since July 2023.
The September move was a quarter point, approved 12 to 0, according to the Fed’s September 16 statement. It put the federal funds rate back where it stood after the October 2025 cut, as the Fed’s target range history on FRED shows.
The year did not start that way. In January two officials voted for a cut. In April four dissented, one for a cut and three against a statement that hinted at cuts, and by July three voted to raise rates while the rest held. Kevin Warsh chaired his first meeting in June, and the September hike was the first rate change under him.

|---|---|

| 2026-07-29 | Hold at 3.50% to 3.75%, vote 9-3. Three preferred a hike. | 
| 2026-09-16 | Raise to 3.75%-4.00%, vote 12-0. | 
| 2026-10-28 | Hold at 3.75% to 4.00%, vote 10-2. | 
How does inflation compare with the Fed’s interest rate?
Inflation is above the Fed’s 2% goal on every measure. Before the decision, September’s consumer price reading of 3.7% sat just under the middle of the Fed’s range. August PCE inflation, the measure used for the Fed’s goal, came in below its September estimate.
The September consumer price index rose 3.7% over the year, up from 3.4% in August. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said gasoline accounted for over half of the monthly increase.
Because the Fed sets a range, we compare inflation with its midpoint, 3.875% going into the meeting. Against September’s CPI the gap is about 0.2 point. Against core PCE inflation it is about 0.9 point; core PCE is the Commerce Department gauge that leaves out food and energy. Neither gap is a Fed threshold; each only describes where the rate sits.
The CPI gap was about 2 points when the last hiking cycle ended in July 2023. Most of the narrowing came from the Fed’s cuts since then, more than from higher inflation, and on core PCE the change is much smaller.

articles.title: Brent crude oil prices rose to $115.98 per barrel following the attack on the refinery. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: Brent crude oil prices rose to $115.98 per barrel following the attack on the refinery.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
Oil prices rose more than 1% in trading on October 28 after an attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery raised concerns about supply risks from the world's leading oil exporter.
 As of 2:47 PM on October 28th, Vietnam time, Brent crude futures rose $2.1, or 1.84%, to $115.98 per barrel. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude also increased $2.1, or 2.1%, to $102 per barrel.
 On October 27, Houthi forces in Yemen announced they had launched a military operation targeting Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, escalating attacks on the world's second-largest crude oil producer. This development caused oil prices to rebound sharply after falling nearly $2 in the previous trading session.
 Experts at ING Bank believe that , at present, oil prices still reflect a high likelihood of a new escalation of tensions.
 ING's team of strategists said oil prices remain pegged at high levels as the market awaits clearer signals on President Donald Trump's next steps regarding Iran.
 These experts predict that if the US election period passes without any new airstrikes against Iran, that could be enough to bring oil prices down.
 Meanwhile, according to data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), US crude oil inventories fell by 2.03 million barrels in the week ending October 23. 
 In addition, the market is also awaiting the meeting of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and its allies, also known as the OPEC+ group. According to informed sources, OPEC+ is expected to maintain its oil production target for December.
 In addition, traders say that crude oil exports from Russia's Baltic and Black Sea ports are likely to fall next month, as Russian refineries increase diesel production following an agreement reached with the US earlier this month.

articles.summary: ECB holds rates at 2.5% on the day Lagarde announces her early exit  Euronews.com
articles.full_text:
The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday, hours after President Christine Lagarde said she would leave next February, months before her term ends, as France's bond market turmoil and inflation at 3.8% cloud the outlook for the eurozone.
The European Central Bank (ECB) left its key deposit rate unchanged at 2.5% on Thursday, at a meeting overshadowed by President Christine Lagarde's announcement earlier in the day that she will leave her post next February, months before her term ends.
The pause comes as a sell-off in French government bonds pushes up borrowing costs across the eurozone, while inflation runs at 3.8%, almost double the ECB's 2% target.
The decision by the Governing Council, which sets interest rates for the 21 countries that use the euro, follows two rate hikes this year, the latest in September, as energy prices linked to the Iran war drove inflation higher. The rates on its main refinancing operations and marginal lending facility also stay at 2.65% and 2.90% respectively.
In its statement, the ECB said energy prices had "continued to rise, posing upside risks to the inflation outlook and downside risks to the growth outlook".
Underlying inflation has "remained broadly stable so far and wages do not show a material response at this stage", it said, but warned that the size and duration of the energy shock were "likely to drive up inflation and lower growth".
The central bank also acknowledged that financing conditions "have tightened since the Governing Council's last meeting, which is likely to weigh on inflation and growth", and repeated that it was "not pre-committing to a particular rate path".
Inflation in the eurozone rose to 3.8% in September, up from 3.2% in August, and the pause had been widely expected.
Lagarde's departure
The meeting came just hours after Lagarde said she would step down on 7 February 2027, around nine months before her eight-year term ends.
The ECB gave no reason, but reports since February have linked the timing to France's presidential election in April 2027.
"I leave this institution with a sense of a good work done and an ECB that is fit for the future," Lagarde said in a separate statement.
Her exit sets off a race to lead the central bank, with Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot seen as frontrunners.
Two other seats on the ECB's six-member Executive Board, including that of chief economist Philip Lane, also open up in the first half of next year.
France in focus
The decision lands in the middle of France's political and fiscal crisis.
French 10-year borrowing costs climbed above 5% last week for the first time since 2002. On Thursday, the yield stood at around 5%, with the gap over German debt at roughly 155 basis points.
Ratings agency Moody’s kept France’s Aa3 rating unchanged last Friday, but with a negative outlook, while a divided parliament struggles to pass next year's budget.
As Euronews reported ahead of the meeting, Dutch bank ING estimated that the rise in bond yields since September had done the work of a 25 basis point hike in Germany, and closer to 50 basis points in France.
"The bond market has taken over the ECB's job," it said in a note.
Lagarde has so far poured cold water on hopes of a rescue. Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, she said that "the primary and first solution lies at home in France. And it has to do with fiscal policies."
In Thursday's statement, the ECB repeated its standard line that the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI), its never-used tool to buy the bonds of countries facing unjustified spikes in borrowing costs, is "available to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics that pose a serious threat to the transmission of monetary policy".
It also left its balance sheet policy untouched, with its bond portfolios still shrinking as it no longer reinvests maturing debt, even though ING had expected a quiet pause in that run-down.

articles.title: Kunlun New Materials HKEX Listing Prospects: Over Half Revenue from CATL – What Are Its Chances of Successful Hong Kong Stock Exchange IPO? - eu.36kr.com
articles.summary: Kunlun New Materials HKEX Listing Prospects: Over Half Revenue from CATL – What Are Its Chances of Successful Hong Kong Stock Exchange IPO?  eu.36kr.com
articles.full_text:
As over half of its revenue relies on CATL, what are the chances that Kunlun New Materials will successfully get listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange?
Kunlun New Materials' long journey to get listed has ushered in new progress.
Huaxia Energy Network has learned that recently, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) disclosed the "Filing Notice for Kunlun New Materials' Overseas Issuance and Listing and Full Circulation of Unlisted Domestic Shares". According to the notice, the company plans to issue no more than 154,159,500 overseas-listed ordinary shares and list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (HKEX).
In January this year, Kunlun New Materials first submitted its listing application to the HKEX. After the first application expired, the company resubmitted the application on August 21. Now, with the completion of the overseas listing filing, Kunlun New Materials has taken another step forward in its listing process.
In fact, Kunlun New Materials has been pursuing this listing dream for several years. As early as June 2023, the company made a sprint for the ChiNext board of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. However, it withdrew its A-share IPO application in less than a year, and the listing plan failed.
Now that the Hong Kong stock listing filing is completed, can Kunlun New Materials fulfill its capital market dream this time?
A Bumpy Road to Listing
Kunlun New Materials' listing journey once had a rather lively opening.
Before Kunlun New Materials officially submitted its A-share listing application, multiple capitals entered the market one after another, and the company's valuation rose accordingly. In August 2021, December 2021 and December 2022, Kunlun New Materials successively received capital increases of 90.5 million yuan, 450 million yuan and 110 million yuan, totaling about 651 million yuan. Calculated based on the share price of each round of capital increase, its post-investment valuation climbed from about 600 million yuan to about 3 billion yuan all the way.
In June 2023, Kunlun New Materials launched an impact on the ChiNext board of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, planning to raise 1 billion yuan, all of which will be invested in the project with an annual output of 240,000 tons of lithium-ion battery electrolyte.
However, before the enthusiasm of capital could be turned into the listing bell-ringing, the industry trend changed.
From 2021 to 2022, the demand for new energy vehicles grew rapidly, the electrolyte was once in short supply, and enterprises expanded production one after another. But as new production capacity was released gradually, industry prices fell and competition intensified.
In the first half of 2023, the average sales price of Kunlun New Materials' electrolyte dropped to 34,600 yuan per ton, which was more than half lower than the 71,800 yuan per ton in 2021. In the same period, operating revenue and net profit decreased by 21.46% and 45.33% year-on-year respectively. In addition, the company's capacity utilization rate also dropped from 91.65% in 2022 to 72.33% in the first half of 2023.
Against this background, Kunlun New Materials even planned to raise funds on the A-share market to expand production. Whether the new production capacity can be digested has become a concern of the industry. At the same time, Kunlun New Materials' low R&D investment has also attracted attention. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange's review inquiry at that time required the company to explain whether the low R&D investment could maintain technological advancement and market competitiveness.
Funds Raised Investment Projects in the ChiNext Prospectus
On May 17, 2024, as Kunlun New Materials and its sponsor withdrew the application, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange terminated its IPO review, and the A-share listing plan was put on hold.
However, the failure in the A-share market did not extinguish Kunlun New Materials' ambition to go public. A year and a half later, Kunlun New Materials decided to move in a different direction to continue its pursuit, so it submitted a listing application to the HKEX in January this year.
CATL Dependency
According to the current prospectus, in the first half of this year, Kunlun New Materials achieved an operating revenue of 1.972 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 209.8%, and its half-year revenue has exceeded the full-year revenue of last year; the net profit attributable to shareholders reached 128 million yuan, compared with a loss of 7.866 million yuan in the same period of the previous year.
Behind the sharp surge in Kunlun New Materials' performance, there is a name that cannot be ignored — CATL (SZ: 300750).
The Hong Kong stock prospectus refers to the company's largest customer as "Group A". Combined with its registered place, listing place and the information disclosed in the previous A-share prospectus, this enterprise is clearly CATL.
Details of Kunlun New Materials' Largest Customer in the First Half of the Year
As early as 2018, the two sides have started cooperation. According to Kunlun New Materials' prospectus, the revenue contributed by CATL accounted for 60.1%, 59.3% and 48.4% respectively from 2023 to 2025. In the first half of this year, the revenue contributed by CATL reached 1.105 billion yuan, accounting for more than half again, reaching 56.1%.
What is more noteworthy is that Kunlun New Materials' dependence on CATL also extends to the procurement side.
In the first half of this year, Kunlun New Materials purchased raw materials such as additives from CATL for an amount of 518 million yuan, accounting for 27.7% of the total procurement amount, making CATL the largest supplier of Kunlun New Materials. The company explained that in order to meet the formula requirements and quality standards of this customer, it needs to purchase specified raw materials from it.
While purchasing raw materials from CATL, it sells products to CATL at the same time. This in-depth cooperation brings order and technical synergy, but also means that Kunlun New Materials is closely linked with the same giant in sales, raw material selection and other links, which carries certain risks.
Speeding up to Catch Up with Industry Leaders
In the electrolyte industry, although Kunlun New Materials ranks high, there is still a noticeable gap compared with the two leading players, Tianci Materials (SZ: 002709) and New Zebang (SZ: 300037).
Calculated based on the electrolyte revenue in 2025, Kunlun New Materials ranks third among global independent electrolyte suppliers, with a market share of 3.6%. In the same period, the shares of Tianci Materials and New Zebang reached 26.8% and 11.8% respectively.
Performance Comparison of Three Major Electrolyte Enterprises in the First Half of the Year
In the first half of this year, Tianci Materials' operating revenue is about 7.5 times that of Kunlun New Materials, and its net profit is 22.4 times that of Kunlun New Materials; New Zebang's operating revenue is about 3.8 times that of Kunlun New Materials, and its net profit is about 7.7 times that of Kunlun New Materials. It can be seen that there are still obvious scale and profit gaps between Kunlun New Materials and the two leading enterprises.
Tianci Materials' advantage is first reflected in its more complete industrial chain layout. Focusing on the electrolyte business, the company has supported the production of key raw materials such as lithium hexafluorophosphate, new electrolytes and additives, and strengthened its cost advantage through the synergy between self-produced raw materials and production links.
New Zebang has a more diverse business portfolio. In addition to battery chemicals, the gross profit margins of electronic information chemicals and organic fluorine chemicals both exceeded 50% in the first half of this year, providing strong support for overall profitability.
Facing the gap, Kunlun New Materials is also accelerating its catch-up, and large-scale production expansion is one of the important steps.
According to the plan disclosed in the August prospectus, the annual electrolyte production capacity of the company's Yichang production base and Jining Production Base II is 100,000 tons and 150,000 tons respectively. The new production capacity added by these two plans alone exceeds the existing annual production capacity of 180,000 tons. After the construction of the new production base or the expansion of production capacity projects are completed, Kunlun New Materials' annual electrolyte production capacity will exceed 500,000 tons.
If it is successfully listed, Kunlun New Materials will obtain more resources to support its catch-up, but the tough battle to catch up with the industry leaders is still ahead.

articles.title: Stablecoins as a vehicle for dollarisation: Evidence from capital controls and currency crises - CEPR
articles.summary: Stablecoins as a vehicle for dollarisation: Evidence from capital controls and currency crises  CEPR
articles.full_text:
Since the US passed the GENIUS Act in July 2025, the stablecoin debate has moved from their role in crypto markets to their potential implications for the international monetary system. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described stablecoins as giving the dollar “an internet-native payment rail that is fast, frictionless, and free of middlemen”, one that will “expand access to the dollar economy for billions across the globe” (Bessent 2025). Other policymakers see risks, particularly for emerging markets. The Bank for International Settlements warns that stablecoins could enable ‘stealth dollarisation’ and capital flight in emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs) (BIS 2025), and recent research has raised similar concerns (Frost et al. 2020, Levy Yeyati and Katz 2025, van 't Klooster et al. 2025, Cecchetti et al. 2026). In an August 2026 speech, IMF First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz laid out both the promise and the risks of stablecoins. Greater competition in payments could lower remittance costs. But stablecoins could also let users sidestep capital flow management measures (CFMs) built around banks and other regulated intermediaries, potentially amplifying outflows in periods of stress. And they could intensify familiar dollarisation pressures, potentially faster and at greater scale than in the past (Katz 2026).
These concerns are hard to assess because stablecoin flows and holdings are largely unmeasured across countries. As Cecchetti et al. (2026) put it, existing balance of payments frameworks “do not capture wallet-based, pseudonymous, cross-border flows”. In this column, I present a new dataset built from blockchain data, document where stablecoins flow and where they are held, and examine how they respond to capital controls and currency crises.
Putting stablecoin flows on the map
Stablecoin transfers are pseudonymous, not anonymous. Every on-chain transfer is recorded on a public blockchain that anyone can read. What the ledger does not show is where senders and receivers are located, because it logs only wallet addresses, which are long strings of letters and numbers. Turning blockchain data into capital flow statistics is therefore a matter of attaching a country to each wallet.
In a new paper (Reuter 2026), I estimate the location of wallets in two steps. First, I build a training set of wallets whose region can be inferred directly. Some wallets carry human-readable domain names, and I use a large language model to infer their region through their linguistic and cultural markers. Other wallets transact almost exclusively with crypto exchanges that serve a single regional market. Together, the two approaches identify the region of hundreds of thousands of wallets. Second, a machine learning model learns how these wallets behave: the hours of the day they are active, whether their activity shifts when daylight saving time begins, and the exchanges and tokens they use. The model then assigns regional probabilities to any sufficiently active wallet. Within each region, I split these probabilities across countries according to where the websites of the exchanges each wallet uses draw their visitors. 
Two external checks support the estimates. Brazil's central bank – to my knowledge the only one that publishes stablecoin transactions with the rest of the world – records residents' purchases of stablecoins from abroad through the foreign exchange payments for them. I estimate the stablecoin side of the same transactions from blockchain data alone, and the two agree within 15%. Internal figures from crypto exchanges, disclosed in enforcement proceedings, sit within a few percentage points of the shares I assign to the US and China. The resulting panel covers USDT and USDC, the two largest stablecoins, in 188 countries, with $21.4 trillion of transfers between 2018 and 2025. Because it records the issuance and redemption of stablecoins, the panel also yields estimates of holdings, not just flows. It is publicly available.
Stablecoin use: Concentrated in emerging markets
Stablecoin flows have grown rapidly. I estimate that transfers exceeded $7 trillion in 2025, up from $1.2 billion in 2018, and that about 90% of this volume crossed borders. Even so, it remains less than 1% of global cross-border payments (Cerutti et al. 2025). The median transfer is $300, closer in size to a remittance than to a wholesale financial transaction. Consistent with Auer et al. (2025), I also find that flows are larger in corridors and quarters in which traditional remittances are more expensive.
The geography of these flows is the reverse of that of traditional payments. Of the volume processed by SWIFT, 85% moves between advanced economies (Basu et al. 2026). In cross-border stablecoin flows, I estimate that only 14% moves between advanced economies, while flows between EMDEs are the largest corridor, at about a third of the total. Relative to GDP, 19 of the 20 largest recipients are EMDEs.
Holdings are also concentrated in EMDEs. I estimate that their holdings more than tripled since the end of 2021, to about $150 billion, raising their share of the roughly $200 billion in stablecoins the panel covers from about half to three quarters (Figure 1). This is consistent with stablecoins serving as a store of value in EMDEs (Adrian et al. 2025, Basu et al. 2026). All twenty of the largest holdings relative to GDP are in EMDEs, led by Venezuela at 5.6% and Ukraine at 4.1%, against 0.04% in the US.
Figure 1 Estimated stablecoin holdings in advanced economies and EMDEs, billions of US dollars
    
  
      
  
Notes: Holdings are approximated by cumulative net flows, including flows from and to stablecoin issuers, split by the estimated location of the holder. The dashed line plots the EMDE share of total holdings (right axis). It briefly exceeds 100% in late 2023, when estimated holdings in advanced economies turn slightly negative. Small negative values reflect coverage gaps and measurement error rather than negative positions. 
Source: Reuter (2026).
Capital controls: Activity rises and persists
Policymakers have worried for several years that crypto assets let residents bypass capital flow management measures (He et al. 2022). The evidence has pulled in two directions. Studies of Bitcoin markets find that crypto is used for capital flight and to evade controls (Hu et al. 2021, Graf von Luckner et al. 2023, 2024). The two studies that look directly at stablecoin flows, however, find little response to restrictions (Auer et al. 2025, Hofmann et al. 2026).
Using the dataset of Bergant et al. (2026a, 2026b), I track 217 activations of capital flow management measures. For each one, I compare the restricting country's cross-border stablecoin activity with that of countries that activate no restriction of their own in the surrounding months. Relative to these countries, activity rises by about 4% in the month the measure takes effect and by roughly 20% within six months (Figure 2, panel a). The response is largest after tightenings of restrictions on capital outflows. It builds to roughly 30% within six months and stays there through the twelfth month (panel b). For the median country, this amounts to about $200 million per month of additional cross-border stablecoin activity. When restrictions are later removed, activity does not detectably fall back, and the data reject the hypothesis that removals undo the initial increase.
Figure 2 Stablecoin activity around new capital flow management measures
    
  
      
  
Notes: Stacked event-study estimates of the change in the restricting country's cross-border stablecoin activity, in log points, relative to the month before the measure takes effect. The comparison group is countries that activate no measure in the surrounding months. Panel (a) pools all 217 activations; panel (b) shows tightenings of outflow restrictions. Shaded areas are 68% and 95% confidence intervals. 
Source: Reuter (2026).
Currency crises: Holdings rise and persist
The second concern is dollarisation. Holding dollars has long been a hedge against depreciation at home, and the dollarisation of bank deposits that crises set off has proved persistent (Reinhart et al. 2014, Valev 2010, Levy Yeyati 2021). I compare 21 countries that entered a currency crisis between 2021 and 2025, dated with the criterion of Laeven and Valencia (2020), with similar EMDEs that did not. Over the year following onset, the crisis countries' combined stablecoin holdings rise by about $7.9 billion relative to the comparison countries, roughly 75% of the $10.4 billion they held before the crisis. Relative to the comparison group, holdings show no significant movement before the crisis, build steadily after onset, and appear to level off after the first year rather than revert (Figure 3). Most of this total comes from the larger crisis economies, and the increase for the median crisis economy is roughly $59 million.
Figure 3 Stablecoin holdings around the onset of currency crises
    
  
      
  
Notes: Stacked event-study estimates of stablecoin holdings in crisis countries, in percentage points of pre-crisis GDP, relative to the month before onset. 21 crises, compared with 86 matched EMDE control countries. Shaded areas are 68% and 95% randomization confidence intervals. 
Source: Reuter (2026).
What the evidence implies
The findings are consistent with both concerns raised in the policy debate. The persistence of both responses also echoes the history of deposit dollarization, which has proved hard to reverse once a crisis set it off (Valev 2010, Levy Yeyati 2021). I find the same pattern for stablecoin holdings after crises, and for stablecoin activity after capital flow restrictions are lifted.
Two qualifications apply. First, the dollar amounts are still moderate. Most of the crises occurred in 2021 and 2022, when the stablecoin market was about half its end-2025 size, and how large the same responses would be in today's

articles.full_text:
The big news for UK-focused investors last week was the Budget. Many investors' worst fears were not realised. CGT rates were not touched, and the tax-free pension sum remained the same. It could be argued that the Chancellor's backtracking on limiting the cash component of an ISA was bad news for the stock market. Still, it also spared investors a complicated reporting system or rules to remember. In many ways this was a goldilocks budget: small, targeted cost-of-living measures may help consumer spending at the margin, but they weren't so generous that bond markets would take fright.
The targeted tax rises did hit some listed companies. Banks face a temporary increase in the bank surcharge from 3% to 6% for 15 months from January 2027. But because the rise was smaller than many investors had feared (reports had suggested 8%), UK bank shares actually rose on the day. Gambling stocks also gained: Machine Games Duty on higher-stakes machines will rise from 20% to 25%, but this was significantly lower than the doubling some had feared.
The net result was a flat FTSE 100 for the week, while smaller UK company indices rose.
The UK 5yr gilt yield retreated from its pre-budget peak and dropped below the psychologically important 5% level.
However, US bond yields also declined during the week, so this may be more a result of global trends than anything UK-specific.
Things have been far less calm for equity markets over the other side of the pond. One headline I read said that Google "crashed" due to concerns that Google's AI-generated summaries and conversational AI Mode are cannibalising traditional search advertising revenue. This certainly looks dramatic on a one-week chart:
However, this is only 12% below where it started the week. Zooming out, the stock has yet to test the April lows, and is 46% above the share price at the start of 2025.
Many of us who tend to focus on smaller companies would love to see this sort of "crash" when our stocks release bad news!
The final market worry of note this week was the hacking of Binance by presumed North Korean hackers, with many describing it as "the largest bank heist in human history". The Binance founder has publicly said that "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss". However, bitcoin's price fell in response. There are a couple of reasons why:
- Binance…

articles.title: EUR/USD Short Squeeze Underway as Yields Drag US Dollar Lower - StoneX
articles.summary: EUR/USD Short Squeeze Underway as Yields Drag US Dollar Lower  StoneX
articles.full_text:
EUR/USD short squeeze gathers pace as US Treasury yields retreat, despite strong GDP and sticky inflation. Fed and ECB policy expectations remain in focus.
EUR/USD is gaining momentum as falling Treasury yields undermine the US dollar, despite stronger GDP growth and stubborn inflation. With record bearish positioning in euro futures and the Fed reluctant to signal further tightening, the short squeeze could have further to run.
Euro Rebounds as Falling Treasury Yields Weigh on the US Dollar
US GDP Accelerates, but Consumer Spending Loses Momentum
The US dollar weakened despite GDP growth accelerating to 3.4% annualised in Q3 and core PCE inflation reaching 3.1% y/y. However, quarterly core inflation eased to 2.5% annualised from 3.3%, while real consumer spending stalled in September despite growing 3.8% annualised over Q3. Real disposable income also fell 0.3% m/m, suggesting households entered Q4 with less spending power.
Treasury yields fell across the curve as bond-market volatility continued to subside. With inflation broadly matching forecasts and the Fed unwilling to commit to further tightening, the data failed to generate a fresh hawkish repricing. Meanwhile, weakness in technology shares may have encouraged demand for Treasuries, adding downward pressure to yields.
ECB Holds Rates, but December Hike Remains in Play
The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% as expected, although the meeting carried a hawkish undertone as rising energy prices increased inflation risks. President Lagarde confirmed policymakers had discussed hiking immediately, but opted to wait for further data amid tighter financing conditions and concerns about economic growth.
A 25bp ECB hike in December now looks increasingly likely, although rising bond yields could limit how far policymakers can tighten thereafter. Market pricing suggests the ECB could tighten slightly faster than the Fed over the near term, although both central banks are expected to deliver around 60bp of cumulative hikes over six months. This leaves EUR/USD sensitive to relative bond yields and positioning, particularly given the sentiment extremes that could leave the euro vulnerable to a short squeeze.
This content was created by an affiliate of FOREX.com and represents the views and opinions of the author/speakers, not the views and opinions of FOREX.com, StoneX Group Inc., or its subsidiaries. The content has not been independently reviewed by FOREX.com.
Falling Treasury yields and bond volatility weigh on the US dollar
Despite stronger US growth and elevated inflation, Treasury yields have fallen sharply from their October highs across the curve. Shorter-dated yields have experienced the largest percentage increases this year, with the two-year up nearly 30%, compared with around 14% for the 10-year and 7% for the 30-year. This has contributed to a substantial flattening of the yield curve, with the 10-year versus two-year spread narrowing to around 33bp from over 100bp earlier this year.
Meanwhile, the MOVE index has fallen towards 95, below its three- and six-month averages, pointing to declining Treasury-market volatility. The combination of falling yields and subdued volatility suggests markets are becoming less concerned about further aggressive tightening, despite stubborn inflation. Demand for Treasuries amid weakness in technology shares may also be contributing to the decline in yields.
The dollar's failure to rally on stronger economic data is therefore telling. For now, falling Treasury yields and a reassessment of the Fed's longer-term policy path appear to be outweighing the hawkish economic headlines. That could bode well for the euro, particularly given the sentiment extremes I previously warned could leave it vulnerable to a short squeeze.
US Dollar Index (DXY) Technical Outlook
The weekly charts shows how the dollar rally has stalled around the upper trend channel – after an inverted hammer candle met resistance around a long-term 50% level. At current prices, the USD index is on track for a shooting star week – which could also be a lower high. And with prices also beneath the May high, perhaps bears could gain some momentum if incoming US data even slightly lowballs.
The daily chart shows the lower more prominently, and bearish momentum is picking up pace. Perhaps a move down to 101 is on the cards, a break beneath which brings the 50-day SMA into focus.
Source: ICE, TradingView
EUR/USD Technical Outlook: Euro vs US Dollar
I sent a couple of reminder heading into the ECB meeting that euro futures were flashing a sentiment extreme.
The most recent Commitment of Traders (COT) report showed that large specs and asset managers had pushed net and gross-short exposure to a record high. Yet the inability for bears to drive EUR/USD beneath the May low to me suggested a crowded trade. And momentum has since turned higher. Given we’re now seeing the US dollar retreat on downwardly revised Fed expectations, the euro could have further to bounce in the coming weeks in my humble opinion.
Source: ICE, TradingView
EUR/USD forecast: All eyes on Warsh at Jackson Hole - Forex Friday
For much of this week, the EUR/USD has been edging lower with the US dollar regaining some ground after last week’s sell-off that was triggered, in part, by the bond market worries. Investors have been unwilling to bet further against the US dollar so far this week ahead of Kevin Warsh’s keynote speech at the Jackson Hole summit, due later today.
DAX and EUR/USD forecast: Lower energy prices, yields offer support
But the question, of course, is how much further oil prices and bond yields can fall. For now, the combination is supportive of risk assets and is helping to sustain a relatively benign decline in the dollar. The focus today will be on US core PCE inflation, due for release shortly, while Nvidia’s second-quarter earnings will provide another test for risk appetite after the US markets close – not just for US indices but for global tech-heavy indices given the influence Nvidia has over the global tech and AI names.

articles.title: US Fed Keeps Rates Unchanged, But December Hike Looms: What It Means For Indian Markets - Outlook Money
articles.summary: US Fed Keeps Rates Unchanged, But December Hike Looms: What It Means For Indian Markets  Outlook Money
articles.full_text:
Summary of this article
- Two Fed policymakers backed a rate hike, keeping December tightening on the table
- Higher US yields could pressure FPI flows, the rupee and Indian equities
- Real estate, IT, aviation and paints face different risks from global developments
The US Federal Reserve has kept interest rates unchanged at 3.75-4 per cent, but two policymakers voted for a hike, keeping the possibility of further monetary tightening in December alive. The decision comes as the Fed weighs persistent inflation against strong economic growth and waits for more data before deciding its next move.
The Fed is also watching the impact of high energy prices, tariffs, strong consumer spending and artificial intelligence (AI)-led investment on inflation. While the September rate hike gave policymakers some room to assess the situation, rising energy costs remain a concern.
Markets are increasingly pricing in another rate hike in December. The CME FedWatch Tool put the probability of a 25-basis-point increase at 79.6 per cent, up from 73.3 per cent a week ago and 49.4 per cent a month earlier.
How A December Fed Rate Hike Could Affect Indian Markets
Higher US interest rates can make dollar assets more attractive to investors, putting pressure on foreign investment flows into emerging markets such as India.
Thomas Priju, portfolio manager at Karma Capital, said the Fed’s decision should not be seen as a positive signal for global equities.
"While the US Federal Reserve has kept interest rates unchanged at 3.75–4.00 per cent, the decision is not necessarily a dovish signal for global equity markets," Priju said. The two votes in favour of a rate hike suggest that inflation remains a concern among Fed policymakers. Priju said the decision to hold rates does not necessarily mean the rate-hiking cycle is over.
"For Indian equities, the implications could be significant. A further increase in US interest rates could keep US bond yields and the dollar elevated, putting pressure on emerging-market capital flows and increasing volatility in the Nifty," he said.
The benchmark US 10-year Treasury Yield has slipped below the key 5 per cent mark, as of 2:30 PM on October 29.
High-valuation stocks and companies that rely heavily on foreign portfolio investment could face greater pressure if global liquidity tightens further. Priju said investors should also keep an eye on domestic earnings and valuations. He advised them to focus on companies with strong earnings visibility and balance sheets, while tracking US inflation data and the Fed’s comments for clues on its next move.
Which Sectors Could Face Pressure
A possible US Fed rate hike could affect Indian sectors differently, depending on their borrowing costs, valuations and exposure to global demand. Sachin Kabra, a Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)-registered investment adviser and co-founder of Foliyo.ai, said the bigger concern for Indian equities was the impact of higher US rates on global capital flows.
"Higher US bond yields make dollar assets more attractive, potentially putting pressure on FPI flows, the rupee and equity valuations," Kabra said.
He said the market reaction would also depend on how much of a potential rate hike was already priced in. A widely anticipated hike could have a limited impact, while an unexpected change in the Fed's outlook could trigger a sharper reaction.
Kabra said rate-sensitive and highly leveraged businesses, particularly real estate, housing finance and certain non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), could face greater pressure if global liquidity tightens. He also flagged companies with expensive valuations but limited earnings visibility as vulnerable.
On the information technology (IT) sector, Kabra said a slowdown in US corporate technology spending could affect demand for discretionary IT services, although a weaker rupee could provide some cushion to Indian exporters. He also said that elevated crude oil prices could pose as an additional risk for Indian companies. With Brent crude trading around $114 per barrel, oil-sensitive sectors such as aviation and paints could face pressure from higher input costs.
Kabra said investors should also watch crude oil prices and the dollar, as both could affect India's inflation outlook and expectations around domestic interest rates.
Should Investors Expect More Volatility Before December
Indian equities could remain volatile in the run-up to the Fed’s December policy decision, particularly as investors react to US inflation readings, bond yields and foreign investment flows.
However, Kabra cautioned against assuming that uncertainty over the Fed’s next move would necessarily trigger a sharp market correction. "The bigger question is whether inflation forces the Fed to remain restrictive for longer than expected," he said.
For Indian investors, this makes the trajectory of US inflation and the Fed’s communication as important as the actual rate decision. A more hawkish outlook than markets anticipate could sustain pressure on emerging-market assets, while a decision that broadly matches expectations may have a more limited impact.
Domestic earnings growth, valuations and investment flows will also determine how Indian equities respond to global developments. Strong domestic fundamentals can offer some support, but they cannot completely insulate markets from changes in global financial conditions.
Kabra advised investors to focus on earnings growth, valuations and asset allocation rather than attempting to predict every Fed decision.

articles.full_text:
- PRESS RELEASE
Results of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters for the fourth quarter of 2026
30 October 2026
- Headline and core inflation expectations revised upwards for 2026 and 2027, owing primarily to higher energy prices and their indirect effects, with longer-term inflation expectations remaining anchored at 2.0%
- Near-term GDP growth expectations revised up, primarily reflecting recent data, with increasing growth continued to be expected in the short run
- Unemployment rate expectations revised up slightly for 2026, but broadly unchanged thereafter
Respondents’ expectations for headline inflation, as measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), stood at 3.0% for 2026, 2.6% for 2027 and 2.0% for 2028. Compared with the previous round, these were revised up by 0.3 and 0.4 percentage points for 2026 and 2027 respectively but remained unchanged for 2028. Longer-term expectations (for 2031) remained at 2.0% for both headline and core inflation. A special question, which was also asked in the previous round, concerned the impact of the war in the Middle East. The responses suggested that additional effects of the energy price shock are mainly expected for 2027 but that second-round effects will remain limited. For inflation, the risk balance was tilted to the upside for 2026-28 but remained more balanced thereafter.
Respondents expected real GDP growth of 1.0% in 2026 and 1.3% in both 2027 and 2028. Expectations were revised up by 0.4 percentage points for 2026 and by 0.1 percentage points for 2027 compared with the previous survey and were unchanged for 2028. Longer-term growth expectations (for 2031) were revised up by 0.1 percentage points to 1.3%. For real GDP growth, the balance of risks was tilted somewhat to the downside for all horizons.
Unemployment rate expectations were slightly higher for 2026 at 6.4%, before declining gradually to 6.1% in the longer term.

articles.title: Chip stocks crash: Intel plunges 30%, AMD drops 12%, Nvidia and Broadcom also slide — what's driving the selloff? - Livemint
articles.summary: Chip stocks crash: Intel plunges 30%, AMD drops 12%, Nvidia and Broadcom also slide — what's driving the selloff?  LivemintSemiconductor Sell-Off: The 1 AI Chip Stock I'd Buy and 1 I'd Avoid  Yahoo FinanceChip Stocks Experienced Their Most Intense Volatility Since 2008. Trade the Rebound or the Retreat With 3X ETFs  Barchart.comBlack Friday Came Early for Chipmakers: Intel and 10 Other Stocks Are More Than 20% Off This Month  TradingViewMarket Take | The C...
articles.full_text:
A multi-fold jump in profits at China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies has triggered another round of selloffs in chip stocks in Friday’s trade on October 30, while disappointing earnings from Amazon and Intel have added to growth concerns on Wall Street.
The losses were led by Intel, which plunged 30%, followed by Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) (12%), Qualcomm (12%), SanDisk (9.7%), Broadcom (5%), Nvidia (4.86%), Micron Technology (4%), and Amazon (2%).
China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) reported a more than sevenfold year-on-year increase in third-quarter revenue to 118.71 billion yuan ($16.7 billion), up 19.3% from the previous quarter, driven by strong demand for memory chips and tight global supplies.
Net profit attributable to shareholders stood at 54.4 billion yuan ($8.17 billion) for the three months ended September 30, compared with a loss in the year-ago period. However, sequential profit growth was more modest at around 3%.
For the first nine months of 2026, revenue reached 269.02 billion yuan, while net profit attributable to shareholders stood at 132.04 billion yuan, reversing a loss of approximately 5.3 billion yuan in the corresponding period last year.
CXMT attributed the improvement to higher memory-chip prices amid tight supply, capacity expansion, and a more favorable product mix.
E-commerce and cloud giant Amazon reported higher-than-expected capital expenditure in the third quarter, alongside slower growth in its online retail business. The company said it spent more than $77 billion on property and equipment in the third quarter, well above analyst expectations, as it continues to expand data centre capacity and meet growing demand for AI services.
Like its competitors, Amazon has also made a massive spending commitment to developing AI software and infrastructure, forecasting capital expenditure of $220 billion this year.
Intel, meanwhile, warned that it would burn cash this year amid a weak PC market, manufacturing bottlenecks, and heavy spending to expand production.
The chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter revenue and profit below Wall Street expectations. PC chips accounted for roughly half of Intel's third-quarter revenue. The company expects sales from the segment to decline by more than 20% sequentially this quarter, following a 5% drop in the September quarter.
The market reacted similarly to Alphabet’s results on Wednesday. The Google parent reported search and advertising sales that reinforced investor concerns about AI’s threat to its core business, sending its shares down 13% at the close Thursday—the biggest drop ever for the stock.
Big Tech deals fail to shield Nasdaq 100 from earnings-driven sell-off
The recent results could be enough to wipe out the Nasdaq 100’s gains at the beginning of this week. The market had initially reacted positively to a slew of big tech news, including Anthropic PBC’s highly anticipated initial public offering filing, Meta Platforms Inc.’s more than $95 billion capital raise, and SpaceX’s $40 billion equipment-finance lease to pay for AI chip purchases.

articles.summary: ExxonMobil Profits Double to $15.4 Billion  Crude Oil Prices Today | OilPrice.comExxon, Chevron profits beat forecasts, refining margins surge during wars  ReutersU.S. Oil Industry Earned Over $130 Billion in Profit During Iran War  The New York TimesEarnings live updates: Exxon, Chevron refining margins jump, lifting earnings  Yahoo FinanceBig Oil is raking in huge profits. Shareholders like Trump are cashing in. You’re paying for it with high gas prices....
articles.full_text:
ExxonMobil reported $15.4 billion in third-quarter profit Friday, more than double its earnings a year earlier, with its Gulf Coast refineries running at full capacity and diesel prices doing the rest.
The company earned $3.72 per share, or $4.23 on an adjusted basis, beating Wall Street's $4.08 estimate. Adjusted net income reached $17.5 billion, making it one of Exxon's most profitable quarters ever.
Exxon's energy products business earned $9.05 billion in adjusted profit, up from $4.1 billion in the second quarter. Its U.S. Gulf Coast refinery units operated at 100% utilization, producing their second-highest diesel volumes on record.
The Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have sidelined roughly 10% of global refining capacity, leaving the remaining plants to supply a market desperately short of diesel and other fuels. Refining margins have soared, and Exxon is certainly making the most of them.
The company has also increased the amount of fuel it can produce. Its Gulf Coast distillate output is up approximately 40% since 2019, helped by the $2 billion Beaumont refinery expansion completed in 2023. That project added 250,000 barrels per day of processing capacity, an investment approved years before today's fuel shortage.
Exxon's upstream business had a less impressive quarter. Adjusted earnings fell to $7.3 billion from $9.2 billion in the second quarter as crude prices eased. Production held near 4.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Exxon generated $25.7 billion in operating cash flow and returned $9.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and stock repurchases, including $5.1 billion in buybacks. It also increased its dividend for the 44th consecutive year and announced plans for another $20 billion in share repurchases in 2027.
With Exxon's Gulf Coast refineries already operating at full capacity, further production increases will be difficult without additional investment. Global diesel supplies remain constrained by refinery damage in the Middle East and Russia, even as crude shipments from the Persian Gulf recover.
